issues.legal_issue: An arbitral award granting extra cartage contrary to a clear contractual allocation of all transportation leads is liable to be set aside when the employer did not require the contractor to obtain materials from the distant source.
material_facts: The contract made the contractor responsible for all leads and provided that the agreed rates applied regardless of the source of materials, provided they met specifications.
The contractor claimed additional payment for transporting stone from a distant source, but the contract contained no separate provision for extra cartage.
There was no evidence that the employer had required the contractor to obtain stone from that distant source.
The arbitrator granted the extra-cartage claims without addressing the contractual term governing all leads and gave no justification for the additional rate.
issues.conclusion: The award on the extra-cartage claims was contrary to the contract and contained an error apparent on its face. The Court allowed the appeal, set aside the Division Bench’s order on those claims, and restored the single Judge’s order setting aside that part of the award.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, a court may set aside an award that is patently illegal or contrary to the contract. An arbitrator must act within the contract and cannot grant relief that a clear and unambiguous term prohibits; an award that plainly disregards such a term may contain an error apparent on its face and be open to court interference. The Court relied on Grid Corporation of Orissa Ltd. v. Balasore Technical School; New India Civil Erectors (P) Ltd. v. Oil & Natural Gas Corporation; Associated Engineering Co. v. Government of A.P.; General Manager, Northern Railway v. Sarvesh Chopra; State of Rajasthan v. Nav Bharat Construction Co.; Hindustan Zinc Ltd. v. Friends Coal Carbonisation; and ONGC Ltd. v. Saw Pipes Ltd. It also referred to Section 28(3), which requires the arbitral tribunal to decide in accordance with the terms of the contract.

rule.if: arbitral_award_challenge and contract_assigns_all_leads_to_contractor and no_employer_required_distant_source and award_ignored_clear_contract_term

predicates.arbitral_award_challenge: The proceeding asks a court to review an arbitral award made under a contract.
predicates.contract_assigns_all_leads_to_contractor: The contract makes the contractor responsible for transportation leads and applies the agreed rates regardless of the source of compliant materials.
predicates.no_employer_required_distant_source: The employer did not require the contractor to obtain the materials from the distant source.
predicates.award_ignored_clear_contract_term: The arbitrator granted extra payment without addressing a clear contractual term governing the relevant cost.

issues.definition: When an arbitral award challenge concerns a contract that assigns all leads to the contractor, the employer did not require a distant source, and the award ignored the clear contractual term, the extra-cartage award is set aside.
